# Upstream merge and inference-regression source audit — round 395

Scope: read-only source/Git audit of `6035c4f92bf87362d7e55051ae1375b9befba89e` in `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-prefill-gated-region-alias-20261013`. No builds, tests, GPU work, implementation, cleanup or Git changes were performed. Existing source refs only; no fetch. The selected tree's version branding does not bound its behavior: `0691bcdf` imports shared upstream code while later local commits add serving, instrumentation and opt-in inference experiments.

## Integration chain and scope

The focused v0.1.43 chain is `33725508` (integration base) → `0691bcdf` (`feat(sycl): import upstream v0.1.43 shared functionality`, official revision `7695859aa13afb248bdb4d36f9b2e95707db079d`) → `f2be61c0` (separate CPU diagnostics/experiment) → later serving/diagnostic/tuning commits → `c617512e` (merge of upstream server branches) → `0f112782` → `6035c4f9`. `c617512e` has server-only source changes: `serve/replicas.py`, admission/affinity, `serve/server.py`, setup and tests/docs. The follow-on `fcb86a77`, `840db05f`, `440e0851`, and `69495a01` likewise adapt server lifecycle, streaming, cache monitor and accounting. The retained server-completion report states engine/build/setup/data sources (318 files) are byte-identical to `0691bcdf`; the server work therefore did not port inference kernels.

`0691bcdf` is wider than a server-only import: 44 files, +10,401/−66. Changes include conversation memory/cache/save-reclaim and session accounting, nonfinite-logit/verification guards, generation error/accounting behavior, OpenAI-facing cache-drop/logit-bias/session-save-retry and context-overflow behavior, setup/benchmark infrastructure. The engine edits are principally correctness, bounds, recovery and shared API/serve requirements (`src/core/conversation_memory.cpp`, `src/core/verify.cpp`, `src/kernels/xe/verify_kernels.cpp`, `src/program/generate.cpp`), plus a host-only session reclaim helper. The diff does not add/change `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2*`, prefill GEMM, XE GEMM kernels, precision defaults, CPU pool policy, or backend selection. These are required functionality/correctness changes, but generation control flow changed and could affect overhead; do not infer zero performance impact without A/B.

`c617512e` is a merge commit with first parent `ee975816` and second parent `de1bfe79`. Its source delta is serving replicas and setup adaptation, not GPU/CPU kernels. Its parent qualification includes fake-engine/HTTP and setup checks; that is functional evidence, not model throughput evidence.

## Optional/local inference and instrumentation changes after the import

* `f2be61c0` is not part of the upstream merge. It adds an opt-in `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_JOB_HISTOGRAM` observer to `src/core/expert_source.cpp` and opt-in `STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU=1` for the narrow IQ3_S NT=1 GU row path in `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2.cpp` / `iq_avx2_rows.inl`. The paired path remains OFF by default. The observer's check is present at native multi-dispatch (`cpu_job_histogram_requested()` then atomic observer load) even when disabled; this is a plausible small CPU hot-path overhead introduced by instrumentation and deserves a paired source comparison. The report `bench/results/2026-10-12-avx2-expert-roofline-and-paired-gu/README.md` records only synthetic per-kernel measurements; paired gathering was ~20% slower for NT=1 GU and rejected; load-sharing was ~3.8% faster in that microcase but varied other cases, default stayed OFF, and whole-model decode improvement was explicitly unverified. No supported claim that this change caused an end-to-end regression.
* `a825e23a` adds a native COPY-only queue behind exact `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1`; current `copy_stream_policy.hpp` caches that opt-in and default is generic queue. `bench/results/2026-10-13-native-copy-queue-tiny-gpu/REPORT.md` reports six tiny lifecycle cases and explicitly no model speed measurement; model path and default remain unqualified/OFF.
* `54385d6f` through `0f112782` add optional phase decode cache ownership/admission and phase-cycle integration. `STRATA_PHASE_DECODE_CACHE` exact `1` is required; phase prefill bounds admit 8192 default or the explicitly guarded 12288 combination, and reject auto chunk in that phase path. The 0f report (`bench/results/2026-10-13-phase-cache-model-lifetime/REPORT.md`) is a lifetime test only, no timing samples, says default OFF. Current HEAD `fd595aa7` / `6035c4f9` add the guarded 12K prefill and gated scratch aliases; `STRATA_PREFILL_SCRATCH_ALIAS` and `STRATA_PREFILL_GATED_ALIAS` are required, with compatibility validation. These are not upstream inference ports and are opt-in, though code-size/branch effects require A/B if performance concern is broad.
* The intermediary prefill service-event, grouped-GEMM, native batching work is diagnostic or source-only; retained reports identify synthetic measurements and no default model speed qualification. Do not treat commit-by-commit proximity as causality.

## Current defaults/flags and benchmark evidence

The current source has phase-cache and native COPY OFF absent explicit environment opt-ins (`phase_serve_cycle.hpp`, `copy_stream_policy.hpp`). MTP requires the explicit `--mtp` option; the retained stock `bench.sh --long --runs 3` control explicitly used no MTP, no batch, no borrow/reuse, 8192 chunk, group16, workers5/tasks18, native IQ3_S. Therefore the measured OFF baseline does not establish performance under a user configuration that turns MTP on. No source evidence here establishes that phase cache or native COPY silently became default-on.

The best in-scope direct stock benchmark is `bench/results/2026-10-13-upstream-benchsh-phase-off-control/REPORT.md`: Arc B570 / Ryzen 5600X, source `0f112782`, input 32049/read with zero reuse, 24 output; prefill 384.8/383.1/386.9 tok/s and decode 7.3/7.8/8.6 tok/s (median 7.8). This is a single 3-run OFF campaign, not an A/B against an earlier candidate. The report says it is not sustained decode, physical 256K or quality qualification. The earlier `33725508`-based official update result is preserved in `bench/results/2026-10-12-upstream-v0143-functional-import-host-qualification/results.json`; it contains prior pristine v0.1.43/xe0.1.42 measurements, but the source/config/measurement identities differ and cannot establish a regression from the current source. The 32K worker reports are also different harness/settings. No matched faster-candidate→current-HEAD end-to-end benchmark was found in this focused chain. Thus “previously faster” is not substantiated by comparable evidence in these records.

## Specific audit questions

* Decode SIMD/native CPU hot paths: upstream `0691bcdf` does not touch them. The distinct `f2be61c0` change adds the paired IQ3_S path gated OFF and observer dispatch check gated OFF; kernel evidence is synthetic only. This is the clearest candidate for a low-cost optional removal/revert test if a CPU-only A/B demonstrates slowdown, but no blanket revert is justified.
* MTP/spec effective flags: the long benchmark control explicitly disables MTP. Engine requires `--mtp`; new MTP opt-ins in `src/core/mtp.cpp` (`STRATA_MTP_*`, coupled/spec paths) are diagnostics/options, not default proof. Compare actual effective startup flags from the allegedly faster run; the report's no-MTP setup does not cover it.
* Phase defaults: exact opt-in `STRATA_PHASE_DECODE_CACHE=1`, OFF by default. Recent phase cache source changes can affect only that opt-in route, except incidental source-size/branch effects.
* COPY queue branch: exact opt-in `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1`, generic fallback by default; tiny GPU lifecycle only, no speed evidence. Do not attribute a decode regression to COPY queue unless the slow run actually selected it.
* CPU dispatch/policy: `f2be61c0` changes observer dispatch instrumentation; paired GU is opt-in. The upstream server merge does not change pool policy, native dispatch selection or CPU affinity in the inference kernel; CPU affinity/replica code is serving resource-management code and only active with replica serving configuration.
* Precision/compiler/backend: the focused v0.1.43 server merges do not alter these inference policies. Current range adds no mandatory change to CUDA/HIP kernels (and this request excludes HIP/CUDA from review). Version strings alone obscure local experiments, but the actual upstream integration diff did not bundle these optional performance paths.

## Safe next comparison and partial-backout candidates

First identify the exact earlier binary and its source/config hashes from existing receipts; then compare same model/provider/compiler/device, same 32K stock request and an identical explicitly recorded MTP setting, same worker/chunk/group/KV settings, same tracing/validation state, alternating OFF/ON source/binary order with individual samples. Separate prefill and decode. Record effective startup flags, whether `STRATA_PHASE_DECODE_CACHE`/`STRATA_COPY_ENGINE` were selected, output count and health/fault state. Existing OFF values above are only a control, not a causal comparison.

If that A/B isolates overhead, reversible partial candidates are: compile-time or runtime eliminate the `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_JOB_HISTOGRAM` instrumentation from native dispatch while retaining any useful qualification report; leave `STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU` disabled (already default); test `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE` and phase cache OFF (already default) against only their actual selected ON treatments. Keep mandatory `0691bcdf` serve/API/security/correctness changes and `c617512e` server functionality. No source removal/backout is recommended from this audit alone; single commits or dissimilar measurements do not prove causality.
